scenes.visual: Title: The Secretory Pathway. Show rough ER, ERGIC, Golgi and cell surface as a route, with a branch to stored granules.

scenes.tts: Cells send newly made proteins to their surface or release them outside. Think of digestive enzymes and hormones. The conventional route starts in the rough endoplasmic reticulum, or E R. Cargo travels through the Golgi, where it is processed and sorted for delivery. This pathway connects protein production to release, either straight away or after storage in a granule.

scenes.visual: Replace the pancreatic timetable with an overview of conventional secretion. Follow yellow cargo from rough ER through ERGIC and Golgi to the surface; preview direct delivery and storage in granules. Label digestive enzymes and hormones as examples. No clocks or numerical timings.

scenes.tts: How do we know the order? A pulse-chase labels newly made protein briefly, then supplies unlabelled amino acid. In guinea-pig pancreas, that labelled cohort moved from rough E R to Golgi to granules. The experiment establishes the order of stops.

scenes.visual: Show a short pulse making yellow labelled proteins, followed by a chase making grey unlabelled proteins. Track the yellow cohort through rough ER, Golgi and granules, using sequential compartment highlights rather than exact arrival times.

scenes.tts: Processing starts in the E R lumen. A core sugar chain is attached, and glucoses are trimmed while the protein folds. Folded cargo passes through the E R G I C to the sis Golgi. Golgi enzymes rebuild the chain in order, adding galactose and sialic acid later.

scenes.visual: Attach a schematic core glycan in the ER lumen and trim glucose tips while cargo folds. Move folded cargo through ERGIC into cis Golgi, then across medial and trans regions. Change the glycan step by step; add labelled galactose and sialic acid tips late. Enzyme regions should overlap rather than form sharp borders.

scenes.tts: E R residents can escape with cargo. The K D E L tag is a return-to-sender label. Its receptor binds escaped residents in the slightly acidic E R G I C and Golgi. Cop one vesicles return them to the E R, where near-neutral conditions let them go. In one model, Golgi enzymes also recycle backward.

scenes.visual: Add a distinct ER-resident protein with a KDEL tag escaping alongside yellow cargo. A receptor binds it in the slightly acidic ERGIC/Golgi; a COPI-coated vesicle returns the complex to ER and releases the resident at near-neutral pH. Also show separate backward arrows recycling Golgi enzymes within the stack.

scenes.tts: In cisternal maturation, a Golgi sac carries cargo while its resident enzymes change. Enzymes recycle backward as the sac changes from early to late. In budding yeast, imaging shows this change directly, with cargo staying inside. Maturation is a leading framework, but no single model explains every observation in the mammalian Golgi.

scenes.visual: Follow one Golgi cisterna containing yellow cargo as early resident markers fade and late markers appear; show resident enzymes returning backward. Then show a scattered budding-yeast cisterna changing early-to-late marker colour while cargo remains inside. Label this as direct yeast evidence. A final mammalian-stack inset states that no single model explains every observation; avoid implying yeast imaging proves an exclusive mammalian mechanism.

scenes.tts: At the trans-Golgi network, the routes split. Constitutive secretion releases protein as fast as it is made. Nearly every eukaryotic cell has this route. Specialized cells also store cargo in granules until a stimulus triggers release. That is regulated secretion. Sorting can continue inside immature granules.

scenes.visual: Branch cargo at the trans-Golgi network. Label a steady stream to the surface constitutive secretion. Label a second branch in specialized cells regulated secretion: immature granules continue sorting, then store concentrated cargo until a stimulus cue triggers fusion and release. Finish with the whole forward route and backward recycling arrows visible.

scenes.tts: A smaller point: Endo H reads part of this processing history. It cuts high-mannose and hybrid sugar chains, but not complex ones. Resistance records passage beyond particular Golgi enzymes. It does not tell you where the protein is now.
